name: IMATINIB
summation:
Imatinib is a Type-2 kinase inhibitor. Its main inhibitory activity is against ABL kinase, but it has significant action at secondary targets including platelet-derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR) and stem cell growth factor receptor (KIT).

Coronavirus: imatinib is reported to block Spike protein-induced SARS-CoV and MERS-CoV fusion in vitro, potentially by blocking Abl2 at the endosomal membrane and disrupting the actin dynamics that are required for virus-host fusion. It will be informative to determine if this holds true for SARS-CoV-2, and whether re-purposing of imatinib and/or newer Abl kinase inhibitors (dasatinib, bosutinib, ponatinib, nilotinib) could be a viable strategy against COVID-19. This approach would likely to be most effective during the early stage of infection.

summation: A single, unpaired primary lymphoid organ situated in the Mediastinum, extending superiorly into the neck to the lower edge of the Thyroid gland and inferiorly to the fourth costal cartilage. It is necessary for normal development of immunologic function early in life. By puberty, it begins to involute and much of the tissue is replaced by fat.

name: Gem
summation: Nuclear bodies frequently found near or associated with Cajal bodies (also called coiled bodies or CBs). Gemini of coiled bodies, or 'gems', are similar in size and shape to CBs, and often indistinguishable under the microscope. Unlike CBs, gems do not contain small nuclear ribonucleoproteins (snRNPs); they contain a protein called survivor of motor neurons (SMN) whose function relates to snRNP biogenesis. Gems are believed to assist CBs in snRNP biogenesis, and to play a role in the etiology of spinal muscular atrophy (SMA)

name: Leishmania promastigote form
summation: The promastigote form of Leishmania is found in the alimentary tract of sandflies. It is an extracellular and motile form. name: Cytokines
summation: Cytokines are a broad and loose category of small proteins (~5–20 kDa) that are important in cell signaling. Cytokines are peptides, and cannot cross the lipid bilayer of cells to enter the cytoplasm. Cytokines have been shown to be involved in autocrine, paracrine and endocrine signaling as immunomodulating agents. Their definite distinction from hormones is still part of ongoing research. Cytokines include chemokines, interferons, interleukins, lymphokines, and tumour necrosis factors, but generally not hormones or growth factors (despite some overlap in the terminology). Cytokines are produced by a broad range of cells, including immune cells like macrophages, B lymphocytes, T lymphocytes and mast cells, as well as endothelial cells, fibroblasts, and various stromal cells; a given cytokine may be produced by more than one type of cell

name: White adipocyte
summation: White fat cells contain a single large lipid droplet surrounded by a layer of cytoplasm, and are known as unilocular.

name: GCG
summation: Glucagon plays a key role in glucose metabolism and homeostasis. Regulates blood glucose by increasing gluconeogenesis and decreasing glycolysis. A counterregulatory hormone of insulin, raises plasma glucose levels in response to insulin-induced hypoglycemia. Plays an important role in initiating and maintaining hyperglycemic conditions in diabetes

name: C1QBP
summation: Complement component 1 Q subcomponent-binding protein, mitochondrial.

name: ABL
summation: Generic representation of Tyrosine-protein kinase ABL1 or ABL2

name: Scavenger receptor class D
summation: Scavenger receptors are a group of receptors that recognize modified low-density lipoprotein

name: CAP
summation: Representation of Adenylyl cyclase-associated protein 1 or 2

name: ROR2/RYK
summation: Representation of Tyrosine-protein kinase transmembrane receptor ROR2 and/or Tyrosine-protein kinase RYK

name: Ragulator
summation: Ragulator complex protein LAMTOR1, LAMTOR2, LAMTOR3, LAMTOR4 and LAMTOR5

name: Plasma cell
summation: Plasma cells, also called plasma B cells, plasmocytes, plasmacytes, or effector B cells, are white blood cells that secrete large volumes of antibodies

name: Keratinocyte
summation: An epidermal cell which synthesizes keratin and undergoes a characteristic change as it moves upward from the basal layers of the epidermis to the cornified (horny) layer of the skin. Successive stages of differentiation of the keratinocytes forming the epidermal layers are basal cell, spinous or prickle cell, and the granular cell.

name: CPSF73
summation: Cleavage and polyadenylation specificity factor subunit 3

name: EPHB
summation: Ephrin type B receptor family member

name: NMDARs
summation: The N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor is a glutamate receptor and ion channel protein found in nerve cells

name: CLR
summation: C-type lectin receptors comprise a large family of receptors that bind to carbohydrates in a calcium-dependent manner. The lectin activity of these receptors is mediated by conserved carbohydrate-recognition domains

name: detailed GPIB-IX-V
summation: Detailed representation of a Glycoprotein Ib-IX-V Receptor Complex.

name: Organism Proteins
summation: Amino acid metabolism provides the precursors for an organism to synthezise and use proteins for a vast array of bodily functions and processes

name: SLC2A4
summation: Solute carrier family 2, facilitated glucose transporter member 4

name: Finger tip section
summation: A segment of a digit containing the distal phalanx, and overlapping the distal interphalangeal joint.

name: Y-Link
summation: Y-Links are protein structures that connect the microtubules from the axonomes to the ciliary membrane.

name: Iron channel
summation: An iron channel is an ion channel which displays selective permeability to iron ions

name: Tropocollagen
summation: Three left-handed procollagens join to form a right-handed triple helical tropocollagen

name: Clostridium tetani
summation: Clostridium tetani is a common soil bacterium and the causative agent of tetanus

name: Symporter 01
summation: A symporter is an integral membrane protein that is involved in the transport of many differing types of molecules across the cell membrane

name: Ligand 03
summation: Substance that forms a complex with a biomolecule to serve a biological purpose. In protein-ligand binding, the ligand is usually a molecule which produces a signal by binding to a site on a target protein

name: Capsid of DENV-2 and ssRNA
summation: Graphical representation of the capsid of a Dengue virus and its ssRNA.

name: Non-Muscle Myosin II
summation: Non-muscle myosin II is an actin-binding protein that has actin cross-linking and contractile properties and is regulated by the phosphorylation of its light and heavy chains

name: Relay neuron
summation: Most generally any neuron which is not motor or sensory

name: Nephron development
summation: Graphic representation of a basic structural and functional unit of the kidney.

name: MAPK1,3
summation: Mitogen-activated protein kinase 1 and 3, also known as ERKs

name: Troponin
summation: Troponin is a complex of three regulatory proteins (troponin C, troponin I, and troponin T) that is integral to muscle contraction in skeletal muscle and cardiac muscle, but not smooth muscle

name: Lysosome
summation: Membrane-bound organelles that are spherical vesicles which contain hydrolytic enzymes that can break down virtually all kinds of biomolecules

name: Pancreatic Ductal Cell
summation: Epithelial cell found in the ducts of the pancreas. This cell type contributes to the high luminal pH.

name: IL-1A
summation: Interleukin 1 alpha (IL-1α) also known as hematopoietin 1 is a cytokine of the interleukin 1 family

name: Retroelement RNA
summation: Mobile genetic element which is transcribed into RNA.

name: eRF1
summation: Eukaryotic peptide chain release factor subunit 1

name: CD40/CD40L
summation: CD40 ligand is a protein that is primarily expressed on activated T cells and is a member of the TNF superfamily of molecules. It binds to CD40 on antigen-presenting cells

name: NADPH oxidase complex
summation: The NADPH oxidase (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate-oxidase) is a membrane-bound enzyme complex that faces the extracellular space. It can be found in the plasma membrane as well as in the membranes of phagosomes used by neutrophil white blood cells to engulf microorganisms

name: Neutrophil
summation: Neutrophils are one of the first-responders of inflammatory cells to migrate towards the site of inflammation

name: ELN:FBN1 aggregate
summation: Graphic representation of the association of elastin (ELN) and fibrillin-1 (FBN1) in the formation of elastic fibers.

name: Follicular dendritic cell
summation: Follicular Dendritic Cells (FDCs) are specialized non-hematopoietic stromal cells of the immune system found in lymph follicules.

name: Megakaryocyte
summation: A megakaryocyte is a large bone marrow cell with a lobulated nucleus responsible for the production of blood platelets

name: Nuclear receptors
summation: Nuclear receptors are a class of proteins found within cells that are responsible for sensing steroid and thyroid hormones and certain other molecules

name: TNFRSF9
summation: Tumor necrosis factor receptor superfamily member 9

name: TBK1
summation: Serine/threonine-protein kinase TBK1 plays an essential role in regulating inflammatory responses to foreign agents

name: GPI TRANSAMIDASE
summation: GPI-anchor transamidase is an enzyme that in humans is encoded by the PIGK gene

name: Scavenger receptor class B
summation: Scavenger receptor class B member 1 (SRB1) also known as SR-BI is a protein that in humans is encoded by the SCARB1 gene. SR-BI functions as a receptor for high-density lipoprotein

name: vif
summation: Counteracts the innate antiviral activity of host APOBEC3F and APOBEC3G

name: MT-ND3
summation: Mitochondrially encoded NADH:ubiquinone oxidoreductase core subunit 3

name: SARS-CoV-1 gRNA coating
summation: Graphic representation of the SARS-CoV 1 gRNA string coating

name: RHO GTPases
summation: The Rho family of GTPases is a family of small (~21 kDa) signaling G proteins. The members of the Rho GTPase family have been shown to regulate many aspects of intracellular actin dynamics, and are found in all eukaryotic kingdoms, including yeasts and some plants

name: RAG1,2
summation: RAG1 and RAG2 are proteins which form a complex to initiate V(D)J recombination and work as endonucleases to cut DNA at certain sites for genetic shuffling.

name: MCM2-7
summation: DNA Replication licensing factor, replicative helicase

name: PRM1,2
summation: Graphic representation of Sperm protamine P1 and Protamine-2

name: Heart
summation: A myogenic muscular circulatory organ found in the vertebrate cardiovascular system composed of chambers of cardiac muscle. It is the primary circulatory organ.

name: Remodeling complex
summation: Subfamily of ATP-dependent chromatin remodeling complexes found in eukaryotes.

name: TCR/MHC I
summation: The T-cell receptor is a molecule found on the surface of T cells that is responsible for recognizing fragments of antigen as peptides bound to MHC class I in this case (major histocompatibility complex) molecules

name: Leishmania amastigote form
summation: The amastigote form of Leishmania is found in the mononuclear phagocytes and circulatory systems of humans. It is an intracellular and nonmotile form, being devoid of external flagella. The short flagellum is embedded at the anterior end without projecting out. It is oval in shape, and measures 3–6 µm in length and 1–3 µm in breadth. The kinetoplast and basal body lie towards the anterior end

name: Selenoproteins
summation: In molecular biology a selenoprotein is any protein that includes a selenocysteine (Sec, U, Se-Cys) amino acid residue. Among functionally characterized selenoproteins are five glutathione peroxidases (GPX) and three thioredoxin reductases, (TrxR/TXNRD) which both contain only one Sec. Selenoprotein P is the most common selenoprotein found in the plasma. It is unusual because in humans it contains 10 Sec residues, which are split into two domains, a longer N-terminal domain that contains 1 Sec, and a shorter C-terminal domain that contains 9 Sec. The longer N-terminal domain is likely an enzymatic domain, and the shorter C-terminal domain is likely a means of safely transporting the very reactive selenium atom throughout the body

name: Cone cell BLUE
summation: One of the two photoreceptor cell types in the vertebrate retina. In cones the photopigment is in invaginations of the cell membrane of the outer segment. Cones are less sensitive to light than rods, but they provide vision with higher spatial and temporal acuity, and the combination of signals from cones with different pigments allows color vision

name: Mammary stem cell
summation: A multi-fate stem cell that is the source of cells for growth of the mammary gland during puberty and gestation. This cell type gives rise to both the luminal and myoepithelial cell types of the gland, and have been shown to have the ability to regenerate the entire organ in mice. This cell type also plays an important role in carcinogenesis of the breast.

summation: Memory B cells are a B cell sub-type that are formed within germinal centers following primary infection and are important in generating an accelerated and more robust antibody-mediated immune response in the case of re-infection

name: PEXIDARTINIB
summation: A pyrrolopyridine that is 5-chloro-1H-pyrrolo[2,3-b]pyridine which is substituted by a [6-({[6-(trifluoromethyl)pyridin-3-yl]methyl}amino)pyridin-3-yl]methyl group at position 3. It is a potent multi-targeted receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitor of CSF-1R, KIT, and FLT3 (IC50 of 20 nM, 10 nM and 160 nM, respectively). Approved by the FDA for the treatment of adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT).

name: Phospholipids
summation: Phospholipids are a class of lipids that are a major component of all cell membranes. They can form lipid bilayers because of their amphiphilic characteristic. The two components are usually joined together by a glycerol molecule. The phosphate groups can be modified with simple organic molecules such as choline, ethanolamine or serine

Some waxes are of mineral origin. Montan wax originates from mob or lignite, that fossilized compound representing a late step of the transformation of vegetal into hydrocarbons

summation: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3-methyl-2-oxovaleric acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group; major species at pH 7.3.

name: AMINES
summation: Compounds and functional groups that contain a basic nitrogen atom with a lone pair

name: Glucose
summation: Glucose is a simple sugar that circulates in the blood of animals as blood sugar

name: all-trans-retinoic acid
summation: A retinoic acid in which all four exocyclic double bonds have E- (trans-) geometry

name: CCA ending
summation: The CCA tail is a cytosine-cytosine-adenine sequence at the 3' end of the tRNA molecule

name: Tripeptides
summation: Any oligopeptide that consists of three amino-acid residues connected by peptide linkages.

name: PYRIMIDINES
summation: One of the three diazines (six-membered heterocyclics with two nitrogen atoms in the ring), it has the nitrogen atoms at positions 1 and 3 in the ring

name: LACTATE
summation: Lactic acid is an organic acid. It has a molecular formula CH3CH(OH)CO2H. It is white in solid state and it is miscible with water. While in liquid state (dissolved state) it is a colorless solution. Production includes both artificial synthesis as well as natural sources. Lactic acid is an alpha-hydroxy acid (AHA) due to the presence of carboxyl group adjacent to the hydroxyl group. It is used as a synthetic intermediate in many organic synthesis industries and in various biochemical industries

name: bHMG-CoA
summation: An acyl-CoA oxoanion that results from the removal of all five protons from the phosphate and carboxylic acid groups of (3S)-3-hydroxy-3-methylglutaryl-CoA.

name: D-ribulose 5’phosphate
summation: The D-enantiomer of ribulose 5-phosphate that is one of the end-products of the pentose phosphate pathway.

name: Lipoxins
summation: Lipoxins (LXs or Lxs), an acronym for lipoxygenase interaction products, are bioactive autacoid metabolites of arachidonic acid made by various cell types. They are categorized as nonclassic eicosanoids and members of the specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) family of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites. Like other SPMs, LXs form during, and then act to resolve, inflammatory responses

name: Altrose
summation: Altrose is an aldohexose sugar. D-Altrose is an unnatural monosaccharide. It is soluble in water and practically insoluble in methanol

name: O-FUCOSYL GROUP
summation: A glycosyl group obtained by removing the hydroxy group from the hemiacetal function of an fucose (6-deoxygalactose) and, by extension, of a lower oligosaccharide having fucose at the reducing end

name: Pentose phosphate
summation: Representation for a phospho sugar that is the phosphate derivative of pentose

name: Adenosine
summation: A ribonucleoside composed of a molecule of adenine attached to a ribofuranose moiety via a β‒N9-glycosidic bond.

name: Triglyceride
summation: A triglyceride (TG, triacylglycerol, TAG, or triacylglyceride) is an ester derived from glycerol and three fatty acids

name: Xylose
summation: Xylose is a sugar first isolated from wood, and named for it. Xylose is classified as a monosaccharide of the aldopentose type, which means that it contains five carbon atoms and includes an aldehyde functional group

name: ESTROGEN
summation: A hormone that stimulates or controls the development and maintenance of female sex characteristics in mammals by binding to oestrogen receptors

name: Ribavirin monophosphate
summation: An organophosphate oxoanion resulting from the removal of both protons from the phosphate group of ribavirin 5'-monophosphate. It is the major species at pH 7.3.

name: Inositol trisphosphate
summation: Inositol trisphosphate or inositol 1,4,5-trisphosphate (abbreviated InsP3 or Ins3P or IP3), together with diacylglycerol (DAG), is a secondary messenger molecule used in signal transduction and lipid signaling in biological cells

name: SEROTONIN
summation: An ammonium ion that is the conjugate acid of serotonin.

name: ORGANIC ANIONS
summation: Organic anions are chemically heterogeneous substances possessing a carbon backbone and a net negative charge

name: Free Fatty Acids
summation: Fatty acids circulating in plasma in their un-esterified form are called free fatty acids. In plasma, FFAs are always bound to a transport protein, usually albumin

name: No motion arrow
summation: An arrow that represents that the motion of a component is not happening due to a disease related process

name: Manganese
summation: A divalent metal cation in which the metal is manganese.

name: Steroids
summation: Any of naturally occurring compounds and synthetic analogues, based on the cyclopenta[a]phenanthrene carbon skeleton, partially or completely hydrogenated; there are usually methyl groups at C-10 and C-13, and often an alkyl group at C-17. By extension, one or more bond scissions, ring expansions and/or ring contractions of the skeleton may have occurred. Natural steroids are derived biogenetically from squalene, so may be considered as triterpenoids

name: Lysophosphatidylglycerol
summation: A glycerophosphoglycerol resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylglycerol, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl

name: Lyxose
summation: Lyxose is an aldopentose — a monosaccharide containing five carbon atoms, and including an aldehyde functional group

name: Hypoxanthine
summation: A purine nucleobase that consists of purine bearing an oxo substituent at position 6.

name: MACR-CoA
summation: Tetraanion of methacrylyl-CoA arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate functions; principal microspecies at pH 7.3.

name: No transformation arrow
summation: An arrow that represents that the transformation of components is not happening due to a disease related process

name: No inhibition arrow
summation: An arrow representing that the inhibition of a component is not happening due to a disease related process

name: APAP-Cys
summation: A cysteine derivative in which the thiol hydrogen of cysteine is replaced by a 5-acetamido-2-hydroxyphenyl group.

name: Sulfate
summation: A sulfur oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of both OH groups of sulfuric acid

name: beta-Alanine
summation: A naturally-occurring β-amino acid comprising propionic acid with the amino group in the 3-position

name: PENTOSES
summation: A pentose is a monosaccharide with five carbon atoms

name: Cob(II)alamin
summation: A cobalamin in which the central cobalt atom has an oxidation state of +2.

name: Homocysteine
summation: A sulfur-containing amino acid consisting of a glycine core with a 2-mercaptoethyl side-chain

name: Acetyl group
summation: The acetyl group contains a methyl group single-bonded to a carbonyl

name: Nucleotide Sugars
summation: Graphic representation of nucleotide sugars which are the activated forms of monosaccharides. Nucleotide sugars act as glycosyl donors in glycosylation reactions. Those reactions are catalyzed by a group of enzymes called glycosyltransferases.

name: bHIB-CoA
summation: An acyl-CoA(−) oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of (S)-3-hydroxyisobutyryl-CoA; principal microspecies at pH 7.3.

name: aKIC
summation: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 4-methyl-2-oxopentanoic acid.

name: Molybdopterin
summation: A molybdopterin that is the O-phospho derivative of [(5aR,8R,9aR)-2-amino-4-oxo-6,7-disulfanyl-3,5,5a,8,9a,10-hexahydro-4H-pyrano[3,2-g]pteridin-8-yl]methanol

name: GLUCURONATE
summation: D-glucuronate can be generated via the degradation of glucuronidated proteins

name: ALDOSTERONE
summation: Aldosterone is a steroid hormone produced by the zona glomerulosa of the adrenal cortex in the adrenal gland

name: Lactose
summation: Lactose is a disaccharide. It is a sugar composed of galactose and glucose

name: Photon
summation: Particle of zero charge, zero rest mass, spin quantum number 1, energy hν and momentum hν/c (h is the Planck constant, ν the frequency of radiation and c the speed of light), carrier of electromagnetic force

name: LIPOYL
summation: Lipoic acid is a sulfur-containing cofactor required for the function of several multienzyme complexes involved in the oxidative decarboxylation of α-keto acids and glycine.

name: Alpha-linoleic acid
summation: A linolenic acid with cis-double bonds at positions 9, 12 and 15. Shown to have an antithrombotic effect

name: Phosphatidylethanolamine
summation: A class of glycerophospholipids in which a phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxy group of ethanolamine

name: Talose
summation: Talose is an aldohexose sugar. It is an unnatural monosaccharide that is soluble in water and slightly soluble in methanol

name: Very Long-Chain fatty acyl-CoA
summation: A fatty acyl-CoA in which the fatty acyl group has a chain length greater than C22

name: PEP
summation: An organophosphate oxoanion obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy and phosphate groups of phosphoenolpyruvic acid.

name: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide oxidized
summation: The oxidised form of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide found in all living cells. In metabolism, NAD+ is involved in redox reactions, carrying electrons from one reaction to another

name: XYLITOL
summation: Xylitol is a sugar alcohol used as a sweetener

name: 2'-0-ACETYL-ADP-RIBOSE
summation: A nucleotide-sugar having ADP as the nucleotide fragment and 2-O-acetyl-D-ribofuranos-5-yl as the sugar component

name: CHOLECALCIFEROL
summation: Cholecalciferol, also known as vitamin D3, is a type of vitamin D which is made by the skin, found in some foods, and taken as a dietary supplement

name: Protectins
summation: The protectin (PD) family of specialized pro-resolving mediators (SPMs) is biosynthesised from docosahexaenoic acid (DHA) and n–3 docosapentaenoic acid (n–3 DPA). All of the PDs show anti-inflammatory and pro-resolving actions

name: ESTRADIOL
summation: Estradiol is an estrogen steroid hormone and the major female sex hormone

name: INORGANIC CATIONS
summation: Ion with fewer electrons than protons, giving it a positive charge

name: Ceramides
summation: Ceramides (N-acyl-sphingoid bases) are a major subclass of sphingoid base derivatives with an amide-linked fatty acid. The fatty acids are typically saturated or monounsaturated with chain lengths from 14 to 26 carbon atoms; the presence of a hydroxyl group on carbon 2 is fairly common. Ceramides are generally precursors of more complex sphingolipids. In the illustrated generalised structure, R1 = OH, OX (where X = acyl, glycosyl, phosphate, phosphonate, etc.), or H

name: Dopaminium
summation: An ammonium ion that is the conjugate acid of dopamine.

name: Isopentenyl diphosphate
summation: A prenol phosphate comprising 3-methylbut-3-en-1-ol having an O-diphosphate substituent

name: Noradrenaline
summation: An organic cation that is the conjugate acid of (R)-noradrenaline, obtained by protonation of the primary amino group.

name: Inositol Phosphates
summation: Inositol phosphates are a group of mono- to polyphosphorylated inositols. They play crucial roles in diverse cellular functions, such as cell growth, apoptosis, cell migration, endocytosis, and cell differentiation

name: Sugars
summation: Sugar is the generic name for sweet-tasting, soluble carbohydrates. They can be simple (monosaccharides such as glucose or fructose), double sugars (disaccharides such as sucrose or maltose) or long chains of sugars (polysaccharides such as starch or glycogen)

name: BILE SALTS
summation: The salt forms of bile acids

name: Amidogen
summation: Amidogen is a radical compound of nitrogen and hydrogen with

name: LPS micelles
summation: Liposaccharide natural compounds consisting of a trisaccharide repeating unit (two heptose units and octulosonic acid) with oligosaccharide side chains and 3-hydroxytetradecanoic acid units.

name: L-valine
summation: An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-valine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: 5'-adenylyl sulfate
summation: An adenosine 5'-phosphate having a sulfo group attached to one the phosphate OH groups.

name: Pseudouridine
summation: An isomer of the nucleoside uridine in which the uracil is attached via a carbon-carbon instead of a nitrogen-carbon glycosidic bond

name: Guanosine
summation: A purine nucleoside in which guanine is attached to ribofuranose via a β-N9-glycosidic bond.

name: VITAMINS
summation: A vitamin is an organic compound and a vital nutrient that an organism requires in limited amounts

name: Ribose
summation: Ribose is an aldopentose that has an aldehyde functional group

name: FMN
summation: A flavin mononucleotide that is riboflavin (vitamin B2) in which the primary hydroxy group has been converted to its dihydrogen phosphate ester

name: Cyanocobalamin

name: Oxaloacetate
summation: Also known as oxaloacetic acid, an oxodicarboxylic acid that is succinic acid bearing a single oxo group

name: Idose
summation: Idose is a hexose, a six carbon monosaccharide. It has an aldehyde group and is an aldose

summation: An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-isoleucine; major species at pH 7.3.

name: Mannose
summation: Mannose is a sugar monomer of the aldohexose series of carbohydrates

name: Malonyl-CoA
summation: The S-malonyl derivative of coenzyme A

name: Glycosylation precursors
summation: Glycosylation precursors are nucleotide-linked sugar donors, synthesized in the cytosol, that take part in the glycosylation of proteins

name: Docosapentaenoic acid
summation: Any straight-chain, C22 fatty acid having five C=C double bonds

name: N-acetylglucosamine
summation: N-acetylglucosamine is a monosaccharide and a derivative of glucose

name: Cobamamide
summation: A member of the class of cobalamins that is vitamin B12 in which the cyano group is replaced by a 5'-deoxyadenos-5'-yl moiety. It is one of the two metabolically active form of vitamin B12

name: N-acetylgalactosamine
summation: N-acetylgalactosamine (GalNAc) is an amino sugar derivative of galactose.

summation: An organophosphate oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate and diphosphate OH groups of NADP+; major species at pH 7.3.

name: Xylulose
summation: Xylulose is a ketopentose, a monosaccharide containing five carbon atoms, and including a ketone functional group

name: URONIC ACIDS
summation: A carbohydrate acid formally derived by oxidation to a carboxy group of the terminal ‒CH2OH group of any aldose or ketose

name: Lysobisphosphatidic acid
summation: A lysophosphatidic acid having the unusual property of a phosphodiester moiety linked to positions sn-1 and sn1' of glycerol; and two additional fatty acids esterified to the glycerol head group

name: Linoleic Acid
summation: An octadecadienoic acid in which the two double bonds are at positions 9 and 12 and have Z (cis) stereochemistry

name: Dolichol
summation: Any one of a group of prenol derivatives made up of varying numbers of cis-linked isoprene units, terminating in an α-saturated isoprenoid group containing an alcohol functional group, with the three isoprene units at the distal end trans-linked.

name: Maltose
summation: Maltose, also known as maltobiose or malt sugar, is a disaccharide formed from two units of glucose joined with an alpha bond. Maltose is the two-unit member of the amylose homologous series, the key structural motif of starch

name: CALCITRIOL
summation: Calcitriol increases the level of calcium (Ca2+) in the blood by increasing the uptake of calcium from the gut into the blood, increasing reabsorption of calcium by the kidneys, and possibly increasing the release of calcium into the blood from bone

name: Hydroxymethyl group
summation: The hydroxymethyl group consists of a methylene bridge bonded to a hydroxy group

name: Polysaccharides
summation: Polysaccharides are polymeric carbohydrate molecules composed of long chains of monosaccharide units bound together by glycosidic linkages and on hydrolysis give the constituent monosaccharides or oligosaccharides

name: Glycosphingolipids
summation: A glycosphingolipid is a glycolipid that is a carbohydrate-containing derivative of a sphingoid or ceramide. It is understood that the carbohydrate residue is attached by a glycosidic linkage to O-1 of the sphingoid

name: N-ribosylnicotinamide
summation: A pyridine nucleoside consisting of nicotinamide with a β-D-ribofuranosyl moiety at the 1-position

name: N-retinylidene-N-retinylethanolamine
summation: A pyridinium ion obtained by formal condensation between two molecules of retinol and one the amino group of ethanolamine. A major constituent of retinal pigment epithelium lipofuscin

name: ORGANIC COMPOUNDS
summation: An organic compound is generally any chemical compound that contains carbon

name: CHOLESTEROL
summation: Cholesterol is a sterol, a type of lipid molecule, and is biosynthesized by all animal cells, because it is an essential structural component of all animal cell membranes; essential to maintain both membrane structural integrity and fluidity

name: 1-acyl-sn-glycero-3-phospho-D-myo-inositol
summation: A 1-acylglycerophosphoinositol in which sn-glycerol, acylated at O1, is linked through a phospho group at O3 to O1 of D-myo-inositol

name: PROTEINS
summation: Proteins are large biomolecules, or macromolecules, consisting of one or more long chains of amino acid residues. Proteins perform a vast array of functions within organisms, including catalysing metabolic reactions, DNA replication, responding to stimuli, and transporting molecules from one location to another

name: Monoglycerides
summation: A glyceride in which any one of the R groups (position not specified) is an acyl group while the remaining two R groups can be either H or alkyl groups

name: Disease releated Inhibition arrow
summation: An arrow representing the inhibition of a component in a disease related process

name: HEME
summation: Heme is a cofactor consisting of an Fe2+ ion contained in the centre of a heterocyclic macrocycle organic compound called a porphyrin, made up of four pyrrolic groups joined together by methine bridges

name: PROGESTERONE
summation: Progesterone is an endogenous steroid and progestogen sex hormone involved in the menstrual cycle, pregnancy, and embryogenesis of humans and other species

name: ISV-CoA
summation: A short chain fatty acyl-CoA(4−) that is the tetraanion of isovaleryl-CoA arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions.

name: 2ʼ-deoxyinosine
summation: A purine 2ʼ-deoxyribonucleoside that is inosine in which the hydroxy group at position 2ʼ is replaced by a hydrogen.

name: Carbamoyl phosphate
summation: A doubly-charged organophosphate oxoanion arising from deprotonation of the phosphate OH groups of carbamoyl phosphate; major species at pH 7.3.

name: Cob(III)alamin
summation: A cobalamin in which the central cobalt atom has an oxidation state of +3.

name: Pro-Inflammatory mediators
summation: These are molecules of different nature such as proteins, peptides, glycoproteins, cytokines, arachidonic acid metabolites (prostaglandins and leukotrienes), nitric oxide, and oxygen free radicals, among others, that are produced by epithelial cells, endothelial cells, or infiltrating inflammatory cells during inflammatory responses

name: CDP-diacylglycerol
summation: A CDP-glycerol having unspecified acyl groups (most commonly fatty acyl groups) at the 1- and 2-positions

name: Metabolites
summation: Any intermediate or product resulting from metabolism. The term 'metabolite' subsumes the classes commonly known as primary and secondary metabolites

name: Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
summation: Glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate, also known as triose phosphate or 3-phosphoglyceraldehyde, is the metabolite that occurs as an intermediate in several central pathways of all organisms

name: Phosphatidylserine
summation: A 3-sn-glycerophosphoserine compound having acyl substituents at the 1- and 2-hydroxy positions.

name: NUCLEOSIDE TRIPHOSPHATES
summation: A nucleoside triphosphate is a molecule containing a nitrogenous base bound to a 5-carbon sugar (either ribose or deoxyribose), with three phosphate groups bound to the sugar

name: D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate
summation: Dianion of D-glyceraldehyde 3-phosphate arising from deprotonation of both OH groups of the phosphate.

name: 2'-o-Methyladenosine
summation: Nucleoside modification in which a methyl grupo is added to the 2' hydroxyl of the ribose moiety of adenosine

name: all-trans-retinol
summation: A retinol in which all four exocyclic double bonds have E- (trans-) geometry

name: Xenobiotics
summation: A xenobiotic (Greek, xenos "foreign"; bios "life") is a compound that is foreign to a living organism. Principal xenobiotics include: drugs, carcinogens and various compounds that have been introduced into the environment by artificial means

name: Resolvins
summation: Resolvins are metabolic byproducts of omega-3 fatty acids, primarily eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) and docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), as well as docosapentaenoic acid (DPA) and clupanodonic acid. As autacoids similar to hormones acting on local tissues, resolvins are under preliminary research for their involvement in promoting restoration of normal cellular function following the inflammation that occurs after tissue injury. Resolvins belong to a class of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites termed specialized proresolving mediators (SPMs)

name: 3'-phospho-5'-adenylyl sulfate
summation: An adenosine bisphosphate having monophosphate groups at the 3'- and 5'-positions and a sulfo group attached to the phosphate at position 5'.

name: sn-glycerol 3-phosphate
summation: An sn-glycerol 3-phosphate having unsubstituted hydroxy groups

name: Urine
summation: GRaphic representation of urine, a liquid containing excess water and water-soluble nitrogen-rich by-products of metabolism including urea, uric acid, and creatinine, which must be cleared from the bloodstream. Urinalysis detects these nitrogenous wastes in mammals.

name: Active Vitamin Forms
summation: Vitamins, which are generally obtained from dietary sources, are converted to their active forms to take part in biochemical processes

name: RETINOL
summation: A retinoid consisting of 3,7-dimethylnona-2,4,6,8-tetraen-1-ol substituted at position 9 by a 2,6,6-trimethylcyclohex-1-en-1-yl group

name: Phosphoinositides
summation: Any phosphatidylinositol that is phosphorylated at one or more of the hydroxy groups of inositol

name: Motion arrow
summation: An arrow that represents the sense of motion

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositols
summation: A phosphatidylinositol in which the inositol moiety is the 1D-myo isomer and the phosphatidyl group is located at its position 1

name: D-erythrose 4-phosphate
summation: D-erythrose 4-phosphate is an erythrose phosphate that is D-erythrose carrying a phosphate group at position 4

name: ISB-CoA
summation: A short chain fatty acyl-CoA(4−) that is the tetraanion of isobutyryl-CoA, arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions.

name: Carbovir Triphosphate
summation: The organic triphosphate that is the 5'-triphosphate of (−)-carbovir

name: CALCIDIOL
summation: Calcidiol is a prehormone that is produced in the liver by hydroxylation of vitamin D3 (cholecalciferol) by the enzyme cholecalciferol 25-hydroxylase

name: Sulfur
summation: Sulfur is a chemical element with the symbol S and atomic number 16. It is abundant, multivalent, and nonmetallic. Under normal conditions, sulfur atoms form cyclic octatomic molecules with a chemical formula S8. Elemental sulfur is a bright yellow, crystalline solid at room temperature

name: Phosphatidic acid
summation: A derivative of glycerol in which one hydroxy group, commonly but not necessarily primary, is esterified with phosphoric acid and the other two are esterified with fatty acids

name: CDP-choline
summation: A member of the class of phosphocholines that is the chloine ester of CDP. It is an intermediate obtained in the biosynthetic pathway of structural phospholipids in cell membranes

name: SORBITOL
summation: Sorbitol, less commonly known as glucitol, is a sugar alcohol with a sweet taste which the human body metabolizes slowly. It can be obtained by reduction of glucose, which changes the aldehyde group to a hydroxyl group

name: all-trans-decaprenyl diphosphate
summation: A decaprenyl diphosphate having (E)-stereochemistry exclusively in the double bonds

name: FARNESYL PP
summation: Farnesyl pyrophosphate is an intermediate in both the mevalonate and non-mevalonate pathways used by organisms in the biosynthesis of terpenes, terpenoids, and sterols

name: 2MBUT-CoA
summation: A 2-methylbutanoyl-CoA(4−) obtained by deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions of (R)-2-methylbutanoyl-CoA; major species at pH 7.3.

name: T3/T4
summation: Graphic representation of 3,3',5'-triiodo-L-thyronine zwitterion and L-thyroxine zwitterion.

name: L-Glutamine
summation: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-glutamine; major species at pH 7.3

name: Disease related Process arrow

name: Galactose
summation: Galactose is a monosaccharide sugar that is about as sweet as glucose

name: NUCLEOTIDES
summation: Nucleotides are organic molecules that serve as the monomer units for forming the nucleic acid polymers DNA and RNA, both of which are essential biomolecules in all life-forms on Earth

name: LIPIDS
summation: 'Lipids' is a loosely defined term for substances of biological origin that are soluble in nonpolar solvents. They consist of saponifiable lipids, such as glycerides (fats and oils) and phospholipids, as well as nonsaponifiable lipids, principally steroids

name: URIC ACID

name: Lysophosphatidylcholine

name: Disaccharides

name: Plasmalogen
summation: Any phospholipid that contains an olefinic function

name: NUCLEOSIDES

name: 2'-o-Methylcytidine

name: bMG-CoA
summation: Pentaanion of trans-3-methylglutaconyl-CoA arising from deprotonation of phosphate, diphosphate and carboxylic acid functions.

summation: Any carboxylic ester obtained by the O-acylation of carnitine

name: L-Asparagine

name: Carboxylases
summation: A class of enzymes that mediate carboxylation reactions

name: Allose

name: Arachidonic Acid
summation: A long-chain fatty acid that is a C20, polyunsaturated fatty acid having four (Z)-double bonds at positions 5, 8, 11 and 14

name: Lysophosphatidylethanolamine
summation: A glycerophosphoethanolamine resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylethanolamine, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl

name: PEPTIDES
summation: Short chains of amino acid monomers linked by peptide (amide) bonds

name: TXA2
summation: A thromboxane which is produced by activated platelets and has prothrombotic properties: it stimulates activation of new platelets as well as increases platelet aggregation

name: 2-oxoglutarate
summation: An oxo dicarboxylate obtained by deprotonation of both carboxy groups of 2-oxoglutaric acid

name: 2-Monolysocardiolipin
summation: A phosphatidylglycerol consisting of cardiolipin lacking one fatty acyl group from the 2 or 2'-position

name: 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin radical cation
summation: An organic radical cation derived from 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin

name: 5mC-DNA
summation: 5-Methylcytosine is a methylated form of the DNA base cytosine that regulates gene transcription and takes several other biological roles.

name: Guanosine monophosphate
summation: Guanosine monophosphate is a nucleotide that is used as a monomer in RNA.

name: HEXOSES
summation: A hexose is a monosaccharide with six carbon atoms

name: MANNITOL
summation: Mannitol is a type of sugar alcohol which is also used as a medication. As a sugar, it is often used as a sweetener in diabetic food, as it is poorly absorbed from the intestines. As a medication, it is used to decrease pressure in the eyes, as in glaucoma, and to lower increased intracranial pressure

name: Propionyl-CoA
summation: An acyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of propionic acid

name: all-trans-retinal
summation: A retinal in which all four exocyclic double bonds have E- (trans-) geometry

name: HA(2)
summation: Hyaluronic acid (HA) is a mucopolysaccharide composed of repeating N-acetylglucosamine and glucuronic acid subunits. HA(2) is a small (800 Da) fragment of HA cleaved from the larger HA(50) fragment which is necessary for HA turnover in the body.

name: 2'-o-Methyluridine
summation: Nucleoside modification in which a methyl grupo is added to the 2' hydroxyl of the ribose moiety of uridine

name: Electrophilic omega 3 oxo-derivatives
summation: Electrophilic oxo-derivatives of ω-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (ω-3 PUFAs) are generated in macrophages and neutrophils in response to inflammation and oxidative stress to promote the resolution of inflammation. Being electrophilic, these derivatives reversibly bind to nucleophilic residues on target proteins, triggering the activation of cytoprotective pathways. These electrophilic derivatives transduce anti-inflammatory actions rather than suppress the production of pro-inflammatory arachidonic acid metabolites

name: Eicosanoids
summation: Eicosanoids are any member of the group of signalling molecules arising from oxidation of the three C20 essential fatty acids (EFAs) icosapentaenoic acid (EPA), arachidonic acid (AA) and dihomo-gamma-linolenic acid (DGLA)

name: Cofactors
summation: An organic molecule or ion (usually a metal ion) that is required by an enzyme for its activity. It may be attached either loosely (coenzyme) or tightly (prosthetic group)

name: Ribonucleotides
summation: Nucleotides containing ribose as its pentose component.

name: Indication arrow
summation: An arrow that indicates or points to something

name: L-Proline
summation: The zwitterion formed from L-proline by proton transfer from the carboxy group to the ring nitrogen. It is the predominant species at physiological pH.

name: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate
summation: Nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide phosphate is a cofactor used in anabolic reactions, such as lipid and nucleic acid synthesis, which require NADPH as a reducing agent

name: AMINO ACIDS
summation: Amino acids are organic compounds containing amine (-NH2) and carboxyl (-COOH) functional groups, along with a side chain (R group) specific to each amino acid

name: Heparan sulfate
summation: Heparan sulfate (HS) is a linear polysaccharide found in all animal tissues. It occurs as a proteoglycan (HSPG) in which two or three HS chains are attached in close proximity to cell surface or extracellular matrix proteins

name: 5' NUCLEOTIDES
summation: Nucleotides are organic molecules that serve as the monomer units for forming the nucleic acid polymers deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) and ribonucleic acid (RNA), both of which are essential biomolecules within all life-forms on Earth. Nucleotides are the building blocks of nucleic acids; they are composed of three subunit molecules: a nitrogenous base, a five-carbon sugar (ribose or deoxyribose), and at least one phosphate group

name: Adenosine triphosphate
summation: A nucleoside triphosphate(4−) obtained by global deprotonation of the triphosphate OH groups of ATP; major species present at pH 7.3.

name: SUCCA
summation: A dicarboxylic acid dianion resulting from the removal of a proton from both of the carboxy groups of succinic acid.

name: L-Citrulline
summation: Zwitterionic form of L-citrulline having an anionic carboxy group and a protonated amino group.

name: Thiamine
summation: Thiamine, also known as thiamin or vitamin B1, is a vitamin found in food, and manufactured as a dietary supplement and medication. Food sources of thiamine include whole grains, legumes, and some meats and fish. Grain processing removes much of the thiamine content, so in many countries cereals and flours are enriched with thiamine. Supplements and medications are available to treat and prevent thiamine deficiency and disorders that result from it, including beriberi and Wernicke encephalopathy. Other uses include the treatment of maple syrup urine disease and Leigh syndrome

name: CORTISOL
summation: Cortisol is a steroid hormone, in the glucocorticoid class of hormones

name: 2MACA-CoA
summation: An acyl-CoA(4−) that is the tetraanion of 2-methylacetoacetyl-CoA, arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions.

name: FATTY ACID
summation: A fatty acid is a carboxylic acid with a long aliphatic chain

name: Carnitine
summation: An amino-acid betaine that is butanoate substituted with a hydroxy group at position C-3 and a trimethylammonium group at C-4

name: Riboflavin
summation: D-Ribitol in which the hydroxy group at position 5 is substituted by a 7,8-dimethyl-2,4-dioxo-3,4-dihydrobenzo[g]pteridin-10(2H)-yl moiety. It is a nutritional factor found in milk, eggs, malted barley, liver, kidney, heart, and leafy vegetables, but the richest natural source is yeast. The free form occurs only in the retina of the eye, in whey, and in urine; its principal forms in tissues and cells are as flavin mononucleotide and flavin-adenine dinucleotide

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol 4,5-bisphosphate
summation: A phosphatidylinositol bisphosphate in which the two phosphate groups are at C-4 and C-5 of the inositol moiety which has the 1D-myo configuration

name: Gulose
summation: Gulose is an aldohexose sugar. It is a monosaccharide that is very rare in nature, but has been found in archaea, bacteria and eukaryotes

name: 2'-deoxyguanosine
summation: A purine 2'-deoxyribonucleoside having guanine as the nucleobase.

name: 1-phosphatidyl-1D-myo-inositol 3-phosphate
summation: A phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate in which the inositol moiety is the D-myo-isomer

name: Inosine monophosphate
summation: A nucleoside 5'-monophosphate(2−) that results from the removal of two protons from the phosphate group of IMP; major species at pH 7.3.

name: bMC-CoA
summation: An acyl-CoA(4−) that is the tetraanion of 3-methylbut-2-enoyl-CoA arising from deprotonation of phosphate and diphosphate functions.

name: Methyl group
summation: A methyl group is an alkyl derived from methane, containing one carbon atom bonded to three hydrogen atoms

name: Citrate
summation: A tricarboxylic acid that is propane-1,2,3-tricarboxylic acid bearing a hydroxy substituent at position 2. It is an important metabolite in the pathway of all aerobic organisms

name: Urea
summation: A carbonyl group with two C-bound amine groups

name: Palmitic acid
summation: Palmitic acid is the most common saturated fatty acid found in animals, plants and microorganisms

name: L-Ascorbate
summation: The L-enantiomer of ascorbate and conjugate base of L-ascorbic acid, arising from selective deprotonation of the 3-hydroxy group. Required for a range of essential metabolic reactions in all animals and plants

name: Lysine
summation: A diamino acid that is caproic (hexanoic) acid bearing two amino substituents at positions 2 and 6

name: Succinyl-CoA
summation: An ω-carboxyacyl-CoA having succinoyl as the S-acyl component

name: Monosaccharide
summation: Monosaccharides, also called simple sugars, are the most basic units of carbohydrates. They are fundamental units of carbohydrates and cannot be further hydrolyzed to simpler compounds

name: Sialic acid
summation: Sialic acid is a generic term for the N- or O-substituted derivatives of neuraminic acid, a monosaccharide with a nine-carbon backbone

name: Tryptophan
summation: L-tryptophan zwitterion. An L-α-amino acid zwitterion obtained by transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tryptophan; major species at pH 7.3

name: Inhibition arrow
summation: An arrow that inhibits the action of a component

name: APAP-GlcA
summation: A beta-D-glucosiduronate that is the conjugate base of acetaminophen O-β-D-glucosiduronic acid, obtained by deprotonation of the carboxy group.

name: ORGANIC ACIDS
summation: An organic acid is an organic compound with acidic properties

name: Prostacyclin
summation: Prostacyclin is a prostaglandin member of the eicosanoid family of lipid molecules

name: Queuosine
summation: Queuosine is a modified nucleoside that is present in certain tRNAs in bacteria and eukaryotes

name: all-trans-retinyl ester
summation: A retintinyl ester in which all double bonds of the retinyl side-chain have trans-configuration

name: Retinoic acid
summation: Retinoic acid is a metabolite of vitamin A or retinol

name: 5,6,7,8-tetrahydrobiopterin
summation: Tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4), also known as sapropterin, is a cofactor of the three aromatic amino acid hydroxylase enzymes, used in the degradation of amino acid phenylalanine and in the biosynthesis of the neurotransmitters serotonin (5-hydroxytryptamine, 5-HT), melatonin, dopamine, norepinephrine (noradrenaline), epinephrine (adrenaline), and is a cofactor for the production of nitric oxide (NO) by the nitric oxide synthases

name: Process arrow
summation: An arrow that represents a single or a multiple processes of one or more elements

name: Metal cations
summation: Metal cations are the result of metal atoms readily losing electrons when undergoing oxidation.

name: Sedoheptulose 7-phosphate
summation: A ketoheptose phosphate consisting of sedoheptulose having a phosphate group at the 7-position. It is an intermediate metabolite in the pentose phosphate pathway.

name: Pantothenic acid
summation: A member of the class of pantothenic acids that is an amide formed from pantoic acid and beta-alanine

name: Ganglioside
summation: A molecule composed of a glycosphingolipid (ceramide and oligosaccharide) with one or more sialic acids linked on the sugar chain

name: 5hmC-DNA
summation: 5-Hydroxymethylcytosine is a DNA pyrimidine nitrogen base derived from cytosine.

name: Lysophosphatidic acid
summation: A member of the class of lysophosphatidic acids obtained by hydrolytic removal of one of the two acyl groups of any phosphatidic acid. A 'closed' class

name: ubiquinol-10
summation: A ubiquinol in which the polyprenyl substituent is decaprenyl

name: Uridine diphosphate
summation: Uridine diphosphate is a nucleotide diphosphate

name: alpha-Linolenoyl-CoA
summation: An octadecatrienoyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of α-linolenic acid

name: 6-TGNs
summation: 6-thioguanine nucleotides (6-TGNs) are the pharmacologically active metabolites of azathioprine.

name: Fatty Alcohols
summation: Fatty alcohols (or long-chain alcohols) are usually high-molecular-weight, straight-chain primary alcohols, but can also range from as few as 4–6 carbons to as many as 22–26, derived from natural fats and oils. The precise chain length varies with the source. Some commercially important fatty alcohols are lauryl, stearyl, and oleyl alcohols. They are colourless oily liquids (for smaller carbon numbers) or waxy solids, although impure samples may appear yellow. Fatty alcohols usually have an even number of carbon atoms and a single alcohol group (–OH) attached to the terminal carbon. Some are unsaturated and some are branched. They are widely used in industry. As with fatty acids, they are often referred to generically by the number of carbon atoms in the molecule, such as "a C12 alcohol", that is an alcohol having 12 carbons, for example dodecanol

name: Coenzyme A
summation: Coenzyme A is a coenzyme, notable for its role in the synthesis and oxidation of fatty acids, and the oxidation of pyruvate in the citric acid cycle

name: 11-cis-retinol
summation: Graphic representation of this kind of retinol

name: Folic acid
summation: An N-acyl-amino acid that is a form of the water-soluble vitamin B9. Its biologically active forms (tetrahydrofolate and others) are essential for nucleotide biosynthesis and homocysteine remethylation

name: No process arrow
summation: An arrow that represents that a single or multiple processes are not happening due to a disease related process

iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: CORIN(802-1042) hydrolyses NPPA to form NPPA(124-151) [plasma membrane, extracellular region]

iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NPPA(124-151) binds NPR1 [extracellular region, plasma membrane]

name: Cob(I)alamin
summation: A cobalamin in which the central cobalt atom has an oxidation state of +1.

name: Adenine
summation: The parent compound of the 6-aminopurines, composed of a purine having an amino group at C-6.

name: COACTIVATORS
summation: A coactivator is a type of transcriptional coregulator that binds to an activator (a transcription factor) to increase the rate of transcription of a gene or set of genes

iconPhysicalEntities.name: NOTCH1 A1701P S2 cleavage fragment
iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NOTCH1 A1701P S2 cleavage fragment [plasma membrane]

iconPhysicalEntities.name: NOTCH1 I1680N S2 cleavage fragment
iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NOTCH1 I1680N S2 cleavage fragment [extracellular region]

iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NOTCH1 I1718T S2 cleavage fragment [extracellular region]

iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NOTCH1 L1678P S2 cleavage fragment [extracellular region]

iconPhysicalEntities.name: NOTCH1 V1676D S2 cleavage fragment
iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: NOTCH1 V1676D S2 cleavage fragment [extracellular region]

name: DHA
summation: A docosahexaenoic acid having six cis-double bonds at positions 4, 7, 10, 13, 16 and 19

name: Selenium
summation: Selenium is a chemical element with the symbol Se and atomic number 34. It is a nonmetal (more rarely considered a metalloid) with properties that are intermediate between the elements above and below in the periodic table, sulfur and tellurium, and also has similarities to arsenic. It rarely occurs in its elemental state or as pure ore compounds in the Earth's crust. Selenium – from Ancient Greek σελήνη (selḗnē) "Moon" – was discovered in 1817 by Jöns Jacob Berzelius, who noted the similarity of the new element to the previously discovered tellurium (named for the Earth)

name: 2'-o-Methylguanosine
summation: Nucleoside modification in which a methyl grupo is added to the 2' hydroxyl of the ribose moiety of guanosine

name: Fructose
summation: Fructose is a simple ketonic monosaccharide found in many plants, where it is often bonded to glucose to form the disaccharide sucrose

name: Thiamine diphosphate
summation: Dianion of thiamine(1+) diphosphate arising from deprotonation of the three OH groups of the diphosphate

name: Linoleoyl-CoA
summation: An octadecadienoyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of linoleic acid

name: Acetyl coenzyme A
summation: Acetyl coenzyme A or acetyl-CoA is a molecule that participates in many biochemical reactions in protein, carbohydrate and lipid metabolism

name: APAP-SO3
summation: Paracetamol sulfate or APAP-SO3 is an aryl sulfate that is paracetamol in which the hydroxy group has been replaced by a sulfooxy group.

name: Reactive oxygen species
summation: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are chemically reactive chemical species containing oxygen. Examples include peroxides, superoxide, hydroxyl radical, and singlet oxygen

name: Glycosaminoglycans
summation: Glycosaminoglycans, GAGs or mucopolysaccharides, are long unbranched polysaccharides consisting of a repeating disaccharide unit

name: GLYCOGEN
summation: Glycogen is a multibranched polysaccharide of glucose that serves as a form of energy storage in humans, animals, fungi, and bacteria. The polysaccharide structure represents the main storage form of glucose in the body

name: Thymidine
summation: Thymidine, or deoxythymidine, is a pyrimidine deoxynucleoside. Deoxythymidine is the DNA nucleoside T, which pairs with deoxyadenosine, A

name: PURINES
summation: Purine is a heterocyclic aromatic organic compound that consists of a pyrimidine ring fused to an imidazole ring

name: Myristoyl group
summation: A straight-chain, fourteen-carbon, long-chain saturated fatty acid mostly found in milk fat

name: NUCLEOSIDE DIPHOSPHATES
summation: A nucleoside diphosphate is a molecule containing a nitrogenous base bound to a 5-carbon sugar with two phosphate groups bound to the sugar

name: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate
summation: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate, DHAP or glycerone phosphate, is an anion involved in many metabolic pathways, including the Calvin cycle in plants and glycolysis

name: Ketone bodies
summation: A carbonyl compound produced as a water-soluble byproduct when fatty acids are broken down for energy in the liver. There are three endogenous ketone bodies: acetone, acetoacetic acid, and (R)-3-hydroxybutyric acid; others may be produced as a result of the metabolism of synthetic triglycerides

name: Odorant particles
summation: Graphic representation of compounds that have an odor

name: Pyridoxal 5'-phosphate
summation: The monophosphate ester obtained by condensation of phosphoric acid with the primary hydroxy group of pyridoxal

name: Acetoacetyl-CoA
summation: A 3-oxoacyl-CoA that results from the formal condensation of the thiol group of coenzyme A with the carboxy group of acetoacetic acid

name: FAD
summation: A flavin adenine dinucleotide in which the substituent at position 10 of the flavin nucleus is a 5'-adenosyldiphosphoribityl group

name: Nascent peptide
summation: Collection of molecules that constitute a ribosome attached to the polypeptide that it is synthesising

name: L-methylmalonyl-CoA
summation: A member of the class of malonyl-CoAs that is malonyl-CoA carrying a methyl group on the malony side chain

name: Lysophosphatidylserine
summation: An acylglycerophosphoserine resulting from partial hydrolysis of a phosphatidylserine, which removes one of the fatty acid groups. The structure is depicted in the image where R1 = acyl, R2 = H or where R1 = H, R2 = acyl. Formula C7H13NO9PR, where R represents the hydrocarbon chain of the fatty acyl group

name: Porphyrins
summation: Porphyrins ( POR-fər-in) are a group of heterocyclic macrocycle organic compounds, composed of four modified pyrrole subunits interconnected at their α carbon atoms via methine bridges (=CH−). The parent porphyrin is porphine, a rare chemical compound of exclusively theoretical interest. Substituted porphines are called porphyrins

name: Fumarate
summation: A hydrogen butenedioate obtained by deprotonation of one of the carboxy groups of fumaric acid

name: Phosphatidylglycerol
summation: A glycerophosphoglycerol that is glycerol in which the hydrogen of one of the primary hydroxy groups has been replaced by a phosphatidyl group

name: Biotin
summation: An organic heterobicyclic compound that consists of 2-oxohexahydro-1H-thieno[3,4-d]imidazole having a valeric acid substituent attached to the tetrahydrothiophene ring. The parent of the class of biotins

name: FADH2
summation: FAD can be reduced to FADH2 through the addition of 2 H+ and 2 e−. FADH2 can also be oxidized by the loss of 1 H+ and 1 e− to form FADH

name: Nicotinic acid D-ribonucleotide
summation: A D-ribonucleotide having nicotinic acid as the nucleobase

name: Ribavirin diphosphate
summation: An organophosphate oxoanion resulting from the removal of the three diphosphate OH groups of ribavirin 5'-diphosphate. It is the major species at pH 7.3.

name: ST metabolites
summation: Graphic representation of metabolites of salicylate.

name: Biocytin
summation: A monocarboxylic acid amide that results from the formal condensation of the carboxylic acid group of biotin with the N6-amino group of L-lysine

name: Maresins
summation: Maresin 1 (MaR1 or 7R,14S-dihydroxy-4Z,8E,10E,12Z,16Z,19Z-docosahexaenoic acid) is a macrophage-derived mediator of inflammation resolution coined from macrophage mediator in resolving inflammation. Maresin 1, and more recently defined maresins, are 12-lipoxygenase-derived metabolites of the omega-3 fatty acid, docosahexaenoic acid (DHA), that possess potent anti-inflammatory, pro-resolving, protective, and pro-healing properties similar to a variety of other members of the specialized proresolving mediators (SPM) class of polyunsaturated fatty acid (PUFA) metabolites

name: APO-CARBOXYLASES
summation: Apo-carboxylases are synthesized as apoenzymes without the coenzyme biotin, which is required for functionality. Once biotin binds to apo-carboxylases, they can catalyze the incorporation of a CO​2 molecule into an organic substrate.

name: AFB1
summation: An aflatoxin having a tetrahydrocyclopenta[c]furo[3',2':4,5]furo[2,3-h]chromene skeleton with oxygen functionality at positions 1, 4 and 11

name: Molybdate
summation: A divalent inorganic anion obtained by removal of both protons from molybdic acid

name: L-Dehydroascorbate
summation: An organic anion and the conjugate base of L-dehydroascorbic acid, arising from deprotonation of the acidic C2-position

name: Polyprenol
summation: A polyprenol in which all linkages of the isoprene units are cis, except for the two furthest from the hydroxy group which are trans.

iconPhysicalEntities.name: pPNOL
iconPhysicalEntities.compartments: cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane
iconPhysicalEntities.displayName: pPNOL [cytoplasmic side of endoplasmic reticulum membrane]

name: Phosphatidylcholine
summation: A glycerophosphocholine that is glycero-3-phosphocholine bearing two acyl substituents at positions 1 and 2

name: Tyrosine
summation: An amino acid zwitterion arising from transfer of a proton from the carboxy to the amino group of L-tyrosine; major species at pH 7.3

name: 2-Monoglyceride
summation: A monoglyceride in which the acyl substituent is located at position 2

name: Dipeptides
summation: Any peptide zwitterion comprising two amino acid residues. Major structure at pH 7.3.

name: Sucrose
summation: Sucrose is common table sugar. It is a disaccharide, a molecule composed of two monosaccharides: glucose and fructose. Sucrose is produced naturally in plants, from which table sugar is refined

name: Carbon monoxide
summation: A one-carbon compound in which the carbon is joined only to a single oxygen. It is a colourless, odourless, tasteless, toxic gas

name: Polyunsaturated fatty acid
summation: Any fatty acid containing more than one double bond. Acids in this group are reported to have cardioprotective effects; and levels are lowered in chronic fatigue syndrome

name: Creatinine
summation: A lactam obtained by formal cyclocondensation of creatine. It is a metabolite of creatine

name: METHIONINE SULFOXIDE
summation: Methionine sulfoxide is an amino acid that occurs naturally although it is formed post-translationally

name: Pyridoxal
summation: A pyridinecarbaldehyde that is pyridine-4-carbaldehyde bearing methyl, hydroxy and hydroxymethyl substituents at positions 2, 3 and 5 respectively. The 4-carboxyaldehyde form of vitamin B6, it is converted into pyridoxal phosphate, a coenzyme for the synthesis of amino acids, neurotransmitters, sphingolipids and aminolevulinic acid

name: Transformation arrow
summation: An arrow that represents a transformation of one or more elements

name: AUG start codon
summation: The start codon is the first codon of a messenger RNA transcript translated by a ribosome

name: 1,2,4-triazole-3-carboxamide
summation: A member of the class of triazoles that is 1H-1,2,4-triazole substituted by an aminocarbonyl group at position 3. It is the major catabolite and aglycon of ribavirin.

name: Mercapturic acids
summation: Mercapturic acid is a condensation product formed from the coupling of cysteine with aromatic compounds. It is formed as a conjugate in the liver and is excreted in the urine. Glutathione-S-transferase adducts lose glutamate and glycine portions, and are acetylated to form mercapturic acids, which are excreted

name: Phosphatidyl-L-serine
summation: A class of aminophospholipids in which a phosphatidyl group is esterified to the hydroxy group of serine

name: MAL
summation: An optically active form of malate having (S)-configuration.

name: Salicylate
summation: A monohydroxybenzoate that is the conjugate base of salicylic acid.

name: aKIV
summation: A 2-oxo monocarboxylic acid anion that is the conjugate base of 3-methyl-2-oxobutanoic acid, arising from deprotonation of the carboxy group.
